proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal C_0\) denote the full literal promise class obtained by imposing \(K_G\leq 0\), without imposing any additional maximum-indegree-three restriction, and let \(\mathcal R_0\) be the subproblem displayed in the statement.  By the definition of \(K_G\),
\[
K_G=\bigl\lvert\{v\in V:\lvert\operatorname{pa}_D(v)\rvert=2\}\bigr\rvert\in\mathbb N_0.
\]
Therefore
\[
K_G\leq 0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad K_G=0.
\]
This equivalence identifies \(\mathcal C_0\) with the full class having no two-parent vertex; it does not impose a bound on vertices having three or more parents and hence does not identify \(\mathcal C_0\) with \(\mathcal R_0\).

Apply \(\mathrm{thm:few\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}parent\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}parameter\mbox{-}hardness}\) at the fixed value \(k=0\).  Its first assertion states that pointwise numerical edge identification on \(K_G\leq 0\), namely on \(\mathcal C_0\), is promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete.  This proves the first assertion of the present theorem.

We next prove the separate assertion about \(\mathcal R_0\).  The same established theorem states that its hardness reduction already lands in the restriction of \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_3\) having \(K_G=0\), rational strictly diagonally dominant positive-definite covariance, and a depth-one directed graph of maximum directed outdegree one whose directed weak components are isolated vertices, single directed edges, or three-parent in-stars.  Every output of that reduction therefore belongs to \(\mathcal R_0\).  Because the source promise problem is promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-hard and the reduction is promise preserving by the cited theorem, \(\mathcal R_0\) is promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-hard.

For membership, the completeness assertion for \(\mathcal C_0\) supplies a polynomial-size universal real predicate for its YES language.  Write that predicate as
\[
U(x)\equiv \forall y\in\mathbb R^r\;\Phi(x,y),
\]
where \(x\) is the finite binary encoding fixed by \(\mathrm{def:promise\mbox{-}problem}\), \(r\) is polynomially bounded in \(\lvert x\rvert\), and \(\Phi\) is the corresponding polynomial-time constructible quantifier-free formula over rational polynomial equalities and inequalities.  Let \(b(x)\) be the Boolean condition that the encoded directed graph has maximum directed indegree at most three and that \(K_G=0\).  Both parts of \(b(x)\) are decidable in polynomial time by counting the incoming entries in each row of the encoded directed adjacency matrix.  Since \(b(x)\) contains no real variable,
\[
b(x)\wedge U(x)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\forall y\in\mathbb R^r\;\bigl(b(x)\wedge\Phi(x,y)\bigr).
\]
Concretely, the polynomial-time formula constructor first evaluates \(b(x)\): if it is true, it outputs \(U(x)\), and if it is false, it outputs the fixed false universal sentence \(\forall y\;(0=1)\).  This realizes the displayed conjunction using only a quantifier-free rational polynomial formula and has polynomial encoding length.  On the promise domain of \(\mathcal R_0\), \(b(x)\) holds and \(U(x)\) is exactly the numerical-identification predicate; outside that promise domain its value is immaterial.  Thus this construction is a valid promise \(\forall\mathbb R\) representation of \(\mathcal R_0\).  Combining membership with the preceding hardness proves that \(\mathcal R_0\) is promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete.  Notice that this argument proves containment and completeness separately and nowhere replaces the full class \(\mathcal C_0\) by \(\mathcal R_0\).

For the algorithmic consequence, suppose that \(\mathsf{ParamHandle}\) yielded an exact algorithm for the full literal parameterized class with bit complexity \(f(k)\operatorname{poly}(n)\).  On \(\mathcal C_0\) one has \(k=0\), so its running time is \(f(0)\operatorname{poly}(n)\).  If \(N\) is the total binary input length, then \(n\leq N\), and hence this is polynomial in \(N\).  It would decide the promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete problem on \(\mathcal C_0\) in polynomial time.  Equivalently, this is the \(k=0\) case of the complexity consequence already established by \(\mathrm{thm:few\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}parent\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}parameter\mbox{-}hardness}\).  Therefore such an algorithm would imply \(\mathsf P=\forall\mathbb R\).

Finally, \(\mathrm{thm:few\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}parent\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}parameter\mbox{-}hardness}\) states that its conclusions concern exact coefficient fibers, including singular fibers, and require no genericity assumption.  Specializing \(k\) to zero and restricting its explicit hard family to \(\mathcal R_0\) changes neither fact.  This proves the final assertion.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For the parameter \(K_G\) as defined, pointwise numerical edge identification on the full literal promise class \(K_G\leq 0\) is promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete.  Indeed, completeness already holds on the more restricted promise subproblem
\[
\mathcal R_0
=
\bigl\{(G,\Sigma,e):(G,\Sigma,e)\text{ lies in the promise domain of }\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_3\text{ and }K_G=0\bigr\}.
\]
Thus \(\mathcal R_0\) is contained in the full literal class at \(k=0\); no equality between these two classes is asserted.  Hence \(\mathsf{ParamHandle}\) cannot yield an \(f(k)\operatorname{poly}(n)\) algorithm for the class stated in the question unless \(\mathsf P=\forall\mathbb R\).  These conclusions hold for exact fibers, including singular fibers, and use no genericity assumption.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The former transition `More precisely' treated the maximum-indegree-three restriction as though it were the full literal class at \(k=0\). The condition \(K_G=0\) excludes only indegree-two vertices and still permits indegree at least four, whereas the subproblem \(\mathcal R_0\) additionally lies in the promise domain of \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_3\). The replacement preserves both true completeness conclusions while making containment, hardness, and membership separate.

proposed.comparator_claim: Proceedings Theorem 2 and Appendix A.1, Corollary 4 of arXiv:2407.12528 construct an exact source-solution-to-fiber isomorphism for rational feasible acyclic instances, but Section 4 stores all source coordinates at one sink whose directed fan-in grows with the source dimension.

Proceedings Theorem 14, numbered Theorem 13 in Appendix A.2 of arXiv:2407.12528, places promise numerical edge identifiability in \(\forall\mathbb R\), and Corollary 5 gives a polynomial-space decision bound.
Theorem 27 gives a correct randomized polynomial-time generic one-, two-, or infinite-identification algorithm for tree-shaped models.
Theorem 1 turns a missing bidirected cycle into a quadratic equation for an incoming directed coefficient.
The main theorem gives an \(O(n^3\log^2 n)\) randomized algorithm for complete generic identification in tree-shaped models.
Theorem 3 equates algebraic MIIV instrumental sets with graphical instrumental sets after latent-to-observed transformation.
Theorem 1 bounds the condition number of bow-free recovery under stated conditioning and diagonal-dominance restrictions.
The paper characterizes graph-wide global identifiability of acyclic linear structural equation models.

The preprint derives influence functions and asymptotic normality for regular half-trek estimators.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The cited membership theorem has different numbering in the official proceedings and arXiv appendix. The replacement names both versions explicitly and also labels the proceedings location for the fiber-isomorphism comparison.

prose_updates.tldr: A covariance-specific coefficient can be generically recoverable yet ambiguous or singular at the supplied covariance. Maximum directed indegree one is the exact tractable side: a deterministic polynomial-bit algorithm normalizes every bi-affine fiber into pole-aware Möbius components and a singular-relation \(2\)-CNF, returning a unique rational coefficient, two unequal feasible witnesses, or a componentwise quadratic nonconstant-curve certificate. At indegree two, promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-completeness already holds for depth-one directed graphs whose directed weak components are isolated vertices, single edges, or two-parent in-stars. Exact-fiber padding gives a hard subproblem \(\mathcal R_0\) inside \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_3\) with \(K_G=0\); the full literal zero-parameter class is larger because \(K_G=0\) does not bound vertices of indegree at least three. The full class is complete by the \(k=0\) specialization of the all-fixed-\(k\) theorem, while \(\mathcal R_0\) is separately complete by the padded reduction and restricted universal-real membership. The private-parent and occurrence-hub compiler is exactly fiber-bijective and has rational strictly diagonally dominant covariance. Dörfler et al. already provide fiber bijectivity; the strict hard-side delta is replacing their shared unbounded-fan-in storage star by components of size at most three.

project_justification.gap: Complete low-fan-in algorithms are generic and may divide by expressions that vanish at the observed covariance. Dörfler et al.'s numerical-hardness construction already gives an exact fiber isomorphism in the rational feasible acyclic mixed-graph class, but its single storage sink has directed fan-in growing with the source dimension; it does not establish hardness on bounded-size directed components. The residual parameter \(K_G\) counts only vertices of indegree exactly two, so the full class \(K_G=0\) may still contain vertices of indegree three or larger and must not be identified with its maximum-indegree-three subproblem.
project_justification.niche: The missing case is an all-covariance, polynomial-bit classification at fan-in one paired with a fiber-faithful lower bound at the next integer fan-in, already on depth-one private-parent components of size at most three, together with an exact audit of the literal parameter that counts only two-parent vertices.
project_justification.fill: The Möbius-component and singular-clause normal form proves exact tractability with checkable componentwise-quadratic certificates. The private-slot compiler replaces the published unbounded storage star by singleton and two-parent sinks, preserves the complete source fiber through forced occurrence hubs, and yields promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-completeness with rational strict diagonal dominance and a planted rational feasible matrix. A polynomial-bit padding preserves the entire fiber and places a hard family in the bounded-fan-in subproblem \(\mathcal R_0\subseteq\{K_G=0\}\). The all-fixed-\(k\) theorem gives completeness of the full literal class, and a separate restriction argument gives membership and completeness of \(\mathcal R_0\).

prose_updates.related_work: Dörfler, van der Zander, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz define numerical edge identification at a feasible covariance, prove unrestricted promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-completeness, and already construct an isomorphism from their source solution set onto the complete real SEM fiber. The membership result is Proceedings Theorem 14 and appears as Theorem 13 in Appendix A.2 of arXiv:2407.12528; Corollary 5 gives the polynomial-space bound. Their Section 4 and Proceedings Theorem 2 use a shared storage sink with one incoming coefficient per source coordinate. The hard-side strict delta here is only the replacement of that unbounded-fan-in star by depth-one private-parent directed components of size at most three while retaining exact fiber bijectivity; rational strict diagonal dominance and a supplied planted witness are normalization properties. The fan-in-one theorem separately tightens their polynomial-space upper bound on that restricted class. The exact padding result supplies a maximum-indegree-three hard subproblem \(\mathcal R_0\) with \(K_G=0\); it does not identify that subproblem with the larger full literal class. Completeness of the full zero-parameter class is the \(k=0\) specialization of the theorem for all fixed \(k\), while completeness of \(\mathcal R_0\) follows separately. Van der Zander, Wienöbst, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz derive missing-cycle quadratic equations and document spurious-root behavior. Gupta and Bläser, followed by Briefs and Bläser, give complete generic algorithms for tree-shaped models; their Möbius and rank analysis informs the pointwise normalization but does not cover exceptional supplied covariances. Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant study graph-wide global identifiability, and Foygel, Draisma, and Drton give the half-trek sufficient criterion for generic rational identification. Ankan, Wortel, Bollen, and Textor connect graphical identification to the MIIVsem workflow, which remains the primary numerical-identification consumer here. Robust recovery, regular half-trek inference, and covariance-confidence-set inversion remain secondary and are not consequences of the exact fiber theorems.
prose_updates.interpretation: The result is a pointwise statement about the structural coefficient \(\lambda_e\), not a claim that a generic formula is numerically safe at every covariance. The observed-law functional is the attainable set \(\mathcal A_e(G,\Sigma)\); the fiber-reduction lemma proves that it equals the set of queried coefficients across all compatible SEM parameterizations, so identification means that this set is a singleton. Fan-in one permits a complete exact audit with constructive low-degree certificates. At fan-in two, hardness persists even though every directed component contains at most one sink and two private roots, so neither long directed paths nor large directed components causes the obstruction. Padding each two-parent sink with one forced-zero private parent preserves the exact fiber and produces a hard subproblem \(\mathcal R_0\) of \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_3\) with \(K_G=0\). This subproblem is contained in, but is not equated with, the full literal zero-parameter class, which may contain vertices of larger indegree. The all-fixed-\(k\) theorem proves completeness of the full class at \(k=0\), and the padded hardness plus restricted universal-real predicate proves completeness of \(\mathcal R_0\). Thus \(K_G\) is not a distance-to-fan-in-one parameter on the literal class. MIIVsem remains the primary applied consumer of the exact audit. Inverting covariance confidence sets can use the audit as a subroutine, but that inferential layer is secondary and is not proved here.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The mathematical proofs cover all singular Möbius branches on the fan-in-one side, every gate, repeated input, copy equation, covariance slot, and selector branch on the hard side, and the complete-fiber padding used for the fixed-\(k\) obstruction. The padded hard subproblem has maximum directed indegree at most three and \(K_G=0\); it is not asserted to equal the full literal zero-parameter class. The presolve computations remain bounded sanity checks rather than an independently audited implementation or machine-checked proof. Certificates are deliberately componentwise quadratic because a single global primitive element can have exponential degree. Numerical stability near poles, approximate covariance input, and finite-sample coverage are outside the exact rational-covariance theorem.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The central exact claims are fully discharged: the fan-in-one real fiber is equivalent to the pole-aware Möbius and \(2\)-CNF normalization, the planted-selector source language has the stated promise completeness, and the private-parent compiler is bijective on the entire compiled coefficient fiber. The indegree-two hard family has directed depth one, maximum directed outdegree one, and directed weak components of size at most three. Exact-fiber padding yields a hard subproblem \(\mathcal R_0\) of maximum directed indegree at most three with \(K_G=0\). The full literal class \(K_G\leq 0\) is larger; its completeness follows by specializing the all-fixed-\(k\) theorem, whereas \(\mathcal R_0\) has a separate membership-and-hardness proof. Remaining audit limitations concern implementation and external verification, not open steps in those proofs: the bounded symbolic checks do not exhaust all rational inputs, and no machine-checked formalization or comprehensive literature audit is claimed. The theorem assumes an exact rational positive-definite covariance and does not establish finite-sample inference, conditioning guarantees near singular strata, covariance-confidence-set coverage, or an exact latent-to-observed fiber bijection. MIIVsem is the intended primary numerical-identification consumer; confidence-set inversion is secondary.

statement_notes.justification: Specializing the established all-fixed-\(k\) theorem at \(k=0\) proves completeness of the full literal class. Its explicit padded hard family proves hardness of the contained subproblem \(\mathcal R_0\), and conjoining the polynomially decidable maximum-indegree-three and \(K_G=0\) checks with the universal-real membership predicate proves membership of that subproblem.
statement_notes.gap: The full literal class with \(K_G=0\) permits vertices of indegree at least three, while \(\mathcal R_0\) lies in the promise domain of \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_3\). The theorem proves both completeness statements separately and makes no equality claim between the classes.
statement_notes.consumer: This is the \(k=0\) corollary of the canonical parameterized maximality theorem and records the stronger fact that a bounded-fan-in subproblem is already complete.
